_: Who the works are. One place, so that adding one is an act of description
rather than an archaeology through eight files.
Everything here is read by the site (assets/site.js, injected when served),
the painting host (art/render.html), the server (/state/meta.json) and the
morning painter (scripts/gen-state.js). A work that is described here and
has a painter is a work the whole site knows about.
canvas      the size the painter composes for. The shape of the work is
this, not a number repeated elsewhere: ratio = w / h.
ground      the colour the work dissolves into when the body falls
silent — its own canvas, sampled from the painting.
silence     'over'   the fade is laid over the finished picture, live,
from today's gap — so it can never be stale;
'within' the work dims from the inside (a pulse inside the
mark) and only its engine can paint it.
listed      false: live and complete, but nothing leads to it and search
engines are told to leave it alone. How a work is watched in
its real conditions before it is shown.
rule        what the page of laws says for this work. `seed` replaces the
seventh law — the one place the works genuinely part.
begun       the day the rule was written — the date of the work. The record it
reads is often older: the body was already keeping it.
unit        what one state of the work is written from: 'day' (default) or 'night'.

archipelago.title: S5-01
archipelago.medium: Software, a sleeping body written nightly by an unchanging rule, screen. Dimensions variable. The rule since 2026, the nights since 2022.

laws: Each night, one painting.
The painting is made from that night’s record of one sleeping body, and from nothing else.
Nothing is arranged by hand.
A night is painted only after the body has woken.
A night is weighed against the nights of this body that came before it, never against the nights that follow.
Several signals drive every visible feature, so that no single one can be read back out.
The hours awake are not drawn. They only part what is drawn.
The instrument’s own verdict on a night is used nowhere in the work.
The seed of a night is drawn from that night’s record alone; the date plays no part in it.
The same night always makes the same painting.
A night that has been painted is never repainted.
When no night arrives, the last painting is held. From the second night of silence it goes out from within.
When the nights resume, the painting returns.
Every night the work has lived is kept.

91.title: S5-03
91.medium: Software, a lived life written daily by an unchanging rule, screen. Dimensions variable. One sheet, the rule since 2026, the days since 2024.

laws: Each day, one painting: one form laid on one sheet.
The form is made from that day's record of one body, and from nothing else.
Nothing is arranged by hand.
The sheet holds every day the body has lived: a new day is laid over the days already there.
A day is weighed against the days of this body that came before it, never against the days that follow.

Each visible feature is driven by one measure of the body, and the rule is published: a measure can be read back out of the sheet, and the work does not pretend otherwise. The sharp points of a day are meant to be read: one point for one hour spent under strain.
The seed of a day is the place its form takes on the sheet; the date only puts the days in order.
The instrument's own verdict on a day is used nowhere in the work.
Where a day falls is the hour the body went to sleep, and how far that hour fell from its own.
The silhouette of a day is cut by the days around it, and only by the days before it.
The same day always makes the same form, and a day once painted is never repainted.
When no day arrives, nothing is laid: the sheet is held, and a long silence fades it.
When the days resume, the first form is written with a doubled channel, and that seam stays on the sheet.
Every day the work has lived is kept, whether or not it can still be seen.
rule.seed: The seed of a day is the place its form takes on the sheet; the date only puts the days in order.

94.title: S6-01
94.medium: Software, lived time written daily by an unchanging rule, screen. Dimensions variable. The rule since 2026, the days since 2022.

laws: Each day, one painting.
The painting is made from that day’s record of one living body, and from nothing else.
Nothing is arranged by hand.
A day is painted only after it has closed.
A day is weighed against the days of this body that came before it, never against the days that follow.
Several signals drive every visible feature, so that no single one can be read back out. The day reaches the brush as five measures of a body, and each is made of at least two ranked signals.
The seed of a day is drawn from the artist’s name, the date, and the day’s record together; no two days can coincide.
Before a mark is made, a body is grown from the five measures. The body is never drawn. It decides where the brush goes.

The brush is an oil brush on an ivory ground, with two palettes and three registers of stroke. It paints three tissues in the order a body is built: the flesh across the whole sheet, the seams of the skin over it, the vessels last and finest.
The same day always makes the same painting.
A day that has been painted is never repainted.
When no day arrives, the last painting is held. From the second day of silence it fades.
When the days resume, the painting returns.
Every day the work has lived is kept.
rule.seed: The seed of a day is drawn from the artist’s name, the date, and the day’s record together; no two days can coincide.
rule.foot:
First recorded day {birth}.

It paints with the brush of S1-01 and parts from it in what is painted: a body grown from the day, which is never shown.

96.title: S6-03
96.medium: Software, ground crossed by a living body and turned by its nights, written daily by an unchanging rule, screen. Dimensions variable. The rule and the days since 2026.

laws: Each day, one painting: the ground the body crossed that day, laid on one sheet.
The painting is made from that day’s record of one living body, where it went, how it moved, how its heart worked and the night that opened the day, and from nothing else.
Nothing is arranged by hand.

The sheet is turned by the body’s nights. Each day adds the turn of the night that opened it: a night calmer than every night before it turns the sheet forty-five degrees clockwise, a faster one forty-five degrees against, the middle night not at all. A day without a recorded night does not turn it.
A day is laid down only after it has closed, at 09:30 the next morning in Barcelona.
The sheet holds every day: the oldest below, the newest on top.
A day is weighed against the days and nights of this body that came before it, never against those that follow.
Each day is fitted to the sheet by its own reach; a day smaller than two hundred metres is not enlarged beyond that.

The turn of a day can be read back as the rank of its night among the nights before it, and the path can be read back as a shape. The width of the stroke cannot: it is the pace woven with the heart, each against that day’s own range.
A circle of two hundred and fifty metres around the house is never written.
The seed of a day is its date; the same day always makes the same painting.
A day that has been painted is never repainted. It loses a twentieth of its presence each day after, and never falls below a twentieth.
A day without a walk lays nothing down. When no day arrives from the instrument, the last sheet is held; from the second day of silence it fades.
Every day the work has lived is kept.
rule.seed: The seed of a day is its date; the same day always makes the same painting.
rule.foot:
First recorded day {birth}.
The rule was written in 2026. The sheet is turned by the body’s nights, not by the calendar.

98.title: S6-05
98.medium: Software, pen and ink on the ground crossed by a living body, written daily by an unchanging rule, screen. Dimensions variable. The rule and the days since 2026.

laws: Each day, one painting: the ground the body crossed that day, written by one pen in one ink.
The painting is made from that day’s record of one living body, where it went, how it moved, how its heart worked and the night that opened the day, and from nothing else.
Nothing is arranged by hand.

The pen writes the way in loops. Where the body moved slowly and its heart worked hard, the loops widen and crowd; where it moved fast, they stretch out. Neither the pace nor the heart can be read back from a loop: each is weighed against that day’s own range, and the two are woven together.
Wherever the body stood for twenty seconds or more, the pen rests and the ink runs as it would run in cloth: the longer the body stood, the wider the stain, up to a limit.
The ink of a day runs from vermilion to carmine: the further its hours lie from the middle of the day and the more height the body climbed, the deeper the red.
The sheet is turned by the body’s nights: each day adds the turn of the night that opened it, up to forty-five degrees either way.
A day is laid down only after it has closed, at 09:30 the next morning in Barcelona.
A day is weighed against its own range and against the nights of this body that came before it, never against those that follow.
A circle of two hundred and fifty metres around the house is never written.
The seed of a day is its date; the same day always makes the same painting.
A day that has been painted is never repainted.
A day without a walk leaves the sheet bare. When no day arrives from the instrument, the last painting is held; from the second day of silence it fades.
Every day the work has lived is kept.
rule.seed: The seed of a day is its date; the same day always makes the same painting.
rule.foot:
First recorded day {birth}.
The rule was written in 2026. It reads the record S6-03 reads and parts from it in what is painted: one day alone, in ink. The cloth is not shown, only the way it took the ink.

99.title: S6-06
99.medium: Software, threads spun from a sleeping body, written nightly by an unchanging rule, screen. Dimensions variable. The rule since 2026, the nights since 2022.

laws: Each night, one painting: one sprout leaves the centre of the sheet and joins every sprout already there.
The painting is made from that night’s record of one sleeping body, and from nothing else.
Nothing is arranged by hand.
A sprout runs further the higher the variability of the heart and the longer the sleep; it runs straighter the lower the resting heart and the nearer the hour of falling asleep came to its habit.

A sprout is spun from many threads. There are more of them after deep sleep and a slow breath; hairs rise along them with movement in sleep and time awake; it branches with dream sleep and with how quickly sleep came.

Along its length each thread follows the phases of the night in their order: deep sleep in dark moss, dream sleep in copper, light sleep in olive, waking in pale lichen. Each phase is stretched by how hard the heart worked during it.
A sprout sets off where the one before it pointed, turned by the warmth of the body and by its breath that night.
No measurement can be read back from a sprout: every feature is woven from two signals, each weighed against the ninety nights of this body that came before it, never against those that follow.
On the morning of its night the new sprout stands at full strength, and every other sprout is dimmed by one step.
No sprout is ever removed. With age a sprout loses its threads and its colour and settles into the felt of the ground.
A night the ring did not record leaves no sprout; an empty grey spore marks its place.
The seed of a night is its date; the same night always makes the same painting.
A night that has been painted is never repainted.
When no night arrives from the instrument, the last painting is held; from the second day of silence it fades.
Every night the work has lived is kept.
rule.seed: The seed of a night is its date; the same night always makes the same painting.
rule.foot:
First recorded night {birth}.
The rule was written in 2026; the nights it reads begin in 2022, because the body had already been recording them. It reads the record S5-01 reads and parts from it in what is painted: not one night alone, but every night the body has slept, gathered into one colony.

100.title: S6-07
100.medium: Software, a cell grown from the day and the night of a living body, written daily by an unchanging rule, screen. Dimensions variable. The rule since 2026, the days since 2022.

laws: Each day, one painting: one cell of cobalt on paper.
The painting is made from that day’s record of one living body, the day itself and the night that opened it, and from nothing else.
Nothing is arranged by hand.

The better the day was for this body, the nearer the cell comes to a circle or an oval. A hard day folds its edge. Night and day weigh equally: the variability of the heart, the length of sleep and the resting heart; the steps, the time spent moving and the time spent sitting.
The edge of the cell is the clock of the day. It is divided by its length into twenty-four equal hours from four in the morning, so the clock holds whatever shape the edge takes.

Rings run outward from the edge. An hour in which the body moved gives more rings, and wider ones; an hour of sitting or sleep gives few and narrow. Where the activity changed often within the hour, their edges fray. Where the ring was taken off, they thin and break.

The cell is filled with fibres. The night lies in it in layers, from falling asleep at the edge to waking at the centre: deep sleep darker, waking lighter, and the layers weigh more the longer the night was.

The fibres are combed by the variability of the heart and the resting heart and lengthened by sleep and calm. Steps and time spent moving thicken them. Restless sleep and a short night leave pale vacuoles.

A day that holds an event this body meets once in several days, a walk of more than an hour and a quarter, twenty thousand steps, a nap of an hour, a practice, opens an island inside the cell, ringed like the cell itself. Its size is the size of the event, weighed by the day.

No measurement can be read back from the cell: every feature is woven from at least two signals, each weighed against the ninety days of this body that came before it, never against those that follow.
A day is laid down only after it has closed, the next morning.
The seed of a day is drawn from that day’s record alone; the date plays no part in it, and the same record always makes the same painting.
A day that has been painted is never repainted.
When no day arrives from the instrument, the last painting is held; from the second day of silence it fades.
Every day the work has lived is kept.
rule.seed: The seed of a day is drawn from that day’s record alone; the date plays no part in it, and the same record always makes the same painting.
rule.foot:
First recorded day {birth}.
The rule was written in 2026; the days it reads begin in 2022, because the body had already been recording them. Before a day leaves the house it is reduced to ranks, the classes of its hours and the phases of its night; no measurement of the body reaches this page.
